evaluations.rationale: Fields to enter are explicitly named (name, optional description); no vague terms that change requirements interpretation.
Specifies inviting by giving a URL; term is concrete and implementation-neutral without causing materially different interpretations.
Specifies 'single multi-line text field' which is concrete and unambiguous for implementation.
Request to 'see all items we try to estimate this session' is clear about scope (this session) and intent.
Selecting an item to estimate/re-estimate is concrete and not open to materially different interpretations.
Adding an item to the list is specific; although wording repeats 'so that', it's not semantically ambiguous.
Editing an item to reflect team's understanding is clear in intent and not materially ambiguous.
Deleting an item from the list is concrete and not open to multiple material interpretations.
'Immediately' is vague here — it could mean automatically on first estimate, on moderator action, or with different timing, which materially affects behavior.
'Average' is ambiguous (arithmetic mean, median, trimmed mean, etc.); different choices yield materially different results.
Condition ('if all estimators show the same card') and outcome (fill estimate field) are explicit and not open to materially different interpretations.
Entering the agreed-upon estimate is explicit and not ambiguous in requirement terms.
Re-estimating a previously estimated story in the session is clear and concrete.
Importing from a spreadsheet is a concrete operation; format/validation details are implementation but the story itself is not materially ambiguous.
Copy/paste from a spreadsheet is a clear, specific action; not open to materially different interpretations.
Browsing previous games to find one is concrete and unambiguous as a user need.
Viewing a transcript of a game is a clear request with little room for materially different interpretations.
Export as an HTML file is specific and unambiguous about format.
Export as CSV is a concrete, well-understood format requirement.
Deleting a game so its stories and estimates are no longer stored is explicit in intent and effect.
Account creation fields (name, email, password, username) are explicitly listed and unambiguous.
Logging in using account name and password is a clear, standard requirement.
'Change my account details' is a high-level intent but not phrased with ambiguous terminology that would produce materially different implementations at this story level.
Deleting an account with the effect described (no longer stored) is explicit and not ambiguous.
Displaying dates/times in local timezone is a clear, testable requirement.
Ambiguous security behavior: could mean sending the actual password, a reminder, or a reset link — materially different and security-relevant.
Provides explicit card sets (examples) and clarifies intent (modified Fibonacci or powers of 2), so interpretation is clear enough for implementation.
Sets a precise numeric limit ('up to 15 estimators') which removes ambiguity despite the descriptive phrase.
Joining by entering a name on the provided URL page is concrete and unambiguous.
Seeing the item being estimated is explicit and leaves little room for materially different interpretations.
Seeing all items for the session is clearly scoped to the session and unambiguous.
'Immediately see that an estimate has been given' implies real-time feedback; while timing expectations exist, it does not create materially different functional interpretations.
Showing all estimates at the same time after all have been given is explicit and unambiguous.
Allows changing estimate up until the last person selects and all are shown — precise stopping condition defined.
Request to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story is specific in scope and meaning.
Seeing who gave what during current round is concrete and not open to multiple material interpretations.
Starting a two-minute countdown visible to all participants is specific and unambiguous.
Resetting the two-minute timer when all play an estimate is a clear trigger and effect.
Scrolling back through prior rounds' stories and estimates is a clearly scoped request.
Requiring consistent card order across draws is explicit and unambiguous for implementation.
Changing estimate while draw not completed is clearly defined by the draw state.
Requesting a small thumbnail photo displayed near cards is a specific UI element; 'small' is a minor presentation detail not causing materially different functional interpretations at story level.
Specifies compliance with XHTML and CSS standards — versions not given but the standards referenced make requirement concrete enough for implementation.
Having a list of definitions for commonly used terms is a clear deliverable and reduces ambiguity rather than introducing it.
Performance goal 'as fast as possible' is vague and could lead to materially different expectations; needs measurable criteria.
Specifies target browsers and versions explicitly, so the requirement is clear and implementable.
'Where possible' is vague and leaves scope of accessibility requirements unspecified, which can materially change implementation.
'Quickly' is an imprecise performance requirement and can lead to materially different implementations without concrete response-time targets.
Support for Unicode is a clear technical capability and not ambiguous.
Terms 'sensible' and 'predictable' are subjective and could be interpreted in materially different ways for URL design.
'Nice' is subjective (design, content, tone) and can lead to differing expectations; needs concrete acceptance criteria.
'Non-identifiable' is ambiguous (anonymized, pseudonymized, aggregated) and has material privacy/technical implications.
'Some metrics' is underspecified (which metrics, granularity, retention), allowing materially different interpretations of what must be delivered.
